private_note: Same numbers as before: Cedar 122, Today 108, Alder 106, Birch 90, Hazel 86. Cedar can't pass, so my real choice is Today versus Alder, and Today is 2 thousand a year better for my household for a generation. Alder may need my vote to pass, but voting for it would mean taking a cut I don't have to take. I won't. Birch and Hazel stay blocked.
statement: I told you in round one what my test was: a plan has to leave my household at least as well off as today. I've stuck to that, and I'll be consistent now. Alder puts the fourth fifth at 106. A deadlock leaves us at 108. That gap is small, and I respect the people who built the Alder coalition. You argued in good faith and you were straight about your interests. But I came here to look after my household and my business, the same as each of you, and Alder asks me to take a cut every year for a generation that I don't have to take. So my final vote is Cedar first, today's arrangements second, then Alder. I will not support Birch or Hazel. If Alder reaches nine without me, so be it. I won't pretend it's a gain for me when it isn't.
